messages:
Morgan: quick idea — can we treat transient GPUs as two tiers instead of 1? cheap-but-volatile and cheap-but-sticky.
Asha: explain sticky vs volatile in practice?
Morgan: volatile = price-optimized spot pools across many zones. sticky = capacity-optimized pools with larger warm buffers and instance types that historically have <1% eviction.
Devin: so sticky costs a bit more but gives fewer interruptions -> fewer fallbacks to on-demand?
Morgan: exactly. our telemetry shows fallback to on-demand is the biggest hidden cost (latency + burst pricing).
Kai: do we have numbers for eviction delta per instance family? can we codify into procurement rules?
Asha: rough numbers: A100-family in us-west2 volatile eviction ~6% last month; some vCPU-GPU combos in us-east1 were ~0.8%. depends on time window.
Morgan: proposal: bidding policy picks price-optimized pools for batch jobs with 30m+ tolerance; capacity-optimized "sticky" pools for low-latency and canary serving. keep 10-15% dedicated reserved buffer for critical namespaces.
Devin: how do we do autoscaling with mixed pools? worry about imbalance if sticky fills slower.
Morgan: autoscaler: prefer sticky until fill threshold, then spillover to volatile. also scale-up warm buffer nodes proactively using time-of-day demand forecast.
Kai: need eviction handling: graceful preemption hook -> drain, KV cache snapshot, fallback route. can we make the handler generic?
Asha: yes. keep snapshot under 2s, use async flush of pre-token cache. add metric: eviction_recovery_time.
Devin: can we simulate expected cost tradeoff? run a week of synthetic traffic against two configs (all-price-optimized vs mixed-tier).
Morgan: I can run sim; quick config outline:
```
# procurement-policy
sticky_pools:
  - family: nvidia-a100
  - strategy: capacity-optimized
  - warm_buffer: 0.12
volatile_pools:
  - families: [nvidia-a10, nvidia-t4]
  - strategy: price-optimized
  - max_bid_pct: 70
fallback:
  on_demand_threshold: 0.02
```

Kai: love the YAML. please add region affinity rules so we don't cross region egress costs during failover.
Asha: and a kill-switch: if eviction_recovery_time > 120s trigger traffic-shift to dedicated nodes.
infra-bot: deploy-check: procurement policy lint passed for draft/mixed-tier-v1 (CI 0.4).
Devin: next steps: Morgan run sim + cost delta, Kai add region affinity constraint, Asha add SLA guardrails.
Morgan: will do. rough ETA 48hrs for sim results.
Kai: ping me when draft PR is up, will review autoscaler hooks.
Asha: nice — this could cut token-cost blowouts during peak by reducing on-demand fallbacks. :thumbsup:
Morgan: cool, posting plan to repo/ops/runbooks once sim done.
Devin: thanks — short sync tomorrow if needed.
